ra: 1 Kings 14:21: Rehoboam reigned in Judah.
1 Kings 15:9-11: Asa king of Judah.
1 Kings 22:41: Jehoshaphat king of Judah.
2 Kings 16:1-2: Ahaz king of Judah.
2 Kings 15:1-2: Azariah/Uzziah king of Judah.
2 Kings 18:1: Hezekiah king of Judah.
2 Kings 21:1: Manasseh king of Judah.
2 Kings 22:1: Josiah king of Judah.
2 Kings 24:18: Zedekiah, last king of Judah.
1 Kings 12:20: Jeroboam made king over Israel.
1 Kings 16:16: Omri king over Israel.
1 Kings 16:29: Ahab king over Israel.
2 Kings 9: Jehu anointed king over Israel.
2 Kings 14:23: Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel.
1 Kings 11:43: Rehoboam son of Solomon succeeded him.
2 Samuel 3:3: Absalom son of David.
1 Samuel 13:16: Jonathan son of Saul.
1 Kings 16:28-29: Ahab son of Omri succeeded him.
2 Kings 20:21: Manasseh son of Hezekiah succeeded him.
1 Kings 16:31: Ahab took Jezebel to wife.
Ruth 4:13: Boaz took Ruth and she became his wife.
Ruth 1:16-18: Ruth clings to Naomi as her mother-in-law and companion.
1 Kings 17-21: Elijah repeatedly confronts Ahab over Baal worship and the Naboth affair.
1 Kings 18-19: Elijah opposes Jezebel, who seeks his life after the Carmel contest.
1 Samuel 17:49-51: David struck down Goliath.
Judges 16: Delilah betrays Samson to the Philistine lords.
2 Samuel 15-18: Absalom rebels against his father David.
2 Kings 25:1-7: Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem and captures and blinds Zedekiah.
2 Kings 5: Naaman cured of leprosy through Elisha's instruction.
2 Kings 19-20: Isaiah delivers Yahweh's word to Hezekiah during the siege and his illness.
Ezra 1:1-4: Cyrus's decree authorizes the return and rebuilding that Ezra advances.
2 Kings 22-23: Josiah's covenant reform exemplifies righteous rule.
1 Kings 21: Jezebel orchestrates false witnesses to seize Naboth's vineyard.
Acts 6:5 names Philip among the Seven; Acts 21:8 calls him 'one of the seven.'
Acts 6:5 lists Stephen first among the Seven; he is the protomartyr.
John 11:1-2: Mary and Martha are the sisters of Lazarus.
Luke 10:38-42; John 11: Mary and Martha are sisters at Bethany.
Galatians 1:19 calls James 'the Lord's brother'; tradition varies on the exact relation.
Mark 6:3 names Judas among the brothers of Jesus; Jude 1:1 calls him 'brother of James.'
Acts 18:2; Romans 16:3: Priscilla and Aquila are a married missionary couple.
Acts 15:40-18:5: Silas a coworker and co-sender with Paul.
1 Corinthians 3:5-9; Acts 18:24-28: Apollos a fellow worker in the Pauline mission.
Romans 16:3: Prisca a 'fellow worker in Christ Jesus.'
Romans 16:3; Acts 18: Aquila a coworker and host of Paul.
Mark 16:1 names Salome among the women who came to anoint Jesus' body.
Eastern tradition counts Mary of Bethany among the myrrh-bearing women.
Mark 16:1; Luke 24:10 name Mary the mother of James among the women at the tomb.
All four Gospels place Mary Magdalene foremost among the myrrh-bearers.
All four Gospels: Pilate is the judge who condemned Jesus to crucifixion.
Matthew 26:57-66; John 11:49-53: Caiaphas presided over the case against Jesus.
Matthew 2: Herod the Great sought the infant Jesus' life (the Massacre of the Innocents).
Mark 6:14-29: Herod Antipas imprisoned and beheaded John the Baptist.
Abu Bakr was the first of the four Rashidun caliphs (632-634 CE).
Umar was the second of the four Rashidun caliphs (634-644 CE).
Uthman was the third of the four Rashidun caliphs (644-656 CE).
Ali was the fourth and last of the Rashidun caliphs (656-661 CE).
Abu Bakr was the closest companion of the Prophet.
Umar was a senior companion of the Prophet.
Uthman was a senior companion and son-in-law of the Prophet.
Ali was a companion, cousin, and son-in-law of the Prophet.
Hamza, the Prophet's uncle, was a companion and martyr of Uhud.
Bilal was an early companion and the first muezzin.
Salman al-Farsi was a companion of the Prophet.
Khalid ibn al-Walid was a companion and commander.
Abu Hurayra was a companion and the foremost hadith narrator.
Zayd ibn Haritha was a companion and adopted son of the Prophet.
Ja'far ibn Abi Talib was a companion and cousin of the Prophet.
Khadijah, the Prophet's first wife, is one of the Mothers of the Believers.
Aisha, a wife of the Prophet, is one of the Mothers of the Believers.
Khadijah was the first wife of the Prophet Muhammad.
Aisha was a wife of the Prophet Muhammad.
Aisha was the daughter of Abu Bakr.
Abu Bakr is named among the Ten Promised Paradise.
Umar is named among the Ten Promised Paradise.
Uthman is named among the Ten Promised Paradise.
Ali is named among the Ten Promised Paradise.
Abd al-Muttalib was the father of Abu Talib.
Abd al-Muttalib was the father of Hamza.
Abu Talib was the father of Ali ibn Abi Talib.
Abu Talib was the father of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib.
Ja'far and Ali were brothers, both sons of Abu Talib.
Khadijah was the mother of Fatima, daughter of the Prophet.
Khalid ibn al-Walid, 'Sword of God,' the foremost general of early Islam.
Hamza, 'Lion of God,' a celebrated warrior.
Abu Hurayra, the foremost transmitter of prophetic knowledge (hadith).
Umar ibn al-Khattab is renowned in tradition for his sense of justice.
Numbers 22-24: Balaam is a diviner/seer who utters true oracles over Israel.
Acts 16:15,40: Lydia hosted Paul and his companions and made her home the base of the Philippian church.
Luke 19:1-10: Zacchaeus received Jesus joyfully and was declared a son of Abraham to whom salvation had come.
John 19:38-42: Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus together took down and buried the body of Jesus.
